parts.ask: Toads N = 900e^(0.12t)/(2e^(0.12t) + 1), t ≥ 0: calculate the number at the start of the study
Find t when there are 420 toads, to 2 d.p.
parts.ms: M1 N = 420 to Ae^(0.12t) = B; A1 60e^(0.12t) = 420; dM1 correct ln work, t = ln 7/0.12; A1 awrt 16.22. Answer without working: SC 1100 (MS p.4)

parts.ask: Explain why, according to the model, the number of toads can never reach 500
parts.ms: B1 upper limit is 450 so cannot reach 500 (or N = 500 gives e^(0.12t) negative, impossible, with conclusion); "the limit is 450" without saying upper limit, or no conclusion, is B0 (MS pp.4–5)

parts.ask: f(x) = 12/(x + 1), x > 0; g(x) = (5/2)ln x, x > 0: find fg(e²) in simplest form
parts.ms: M1 g first: f((5/2)ln e²) = f(5); A1 cso 2 (MS p.6)

parts.ask: Find f⁻¹
parts.ms: M1 change the subject; A1 f⁻¹(x) = 12/x − 1 or (12 − x)/x with correct notation (f⁻¹ = … incomplete, A0); B1 0 < x < 12 (MS pp.6–7)

parts.ask: Hence or otherwise find all real solutions of f⁻¹(x) = f(x)
parts.ms: M1 set f⁻¹(x) = f(x) (or f(x) = x) and reach a quadratic; dM1 solve x² + x − 12 = 0; A1 x = 3 only (MS pp.6–7)

parts.ask: log₁₀y against log₁₀x is a line through (0, 4) and (6, 0): find an equation linking log₁₀y and log₁₀x
parts.ms: M1 form ±(2/3)log₁₀x + 4; A1 log₁₀y = −(2/3)log₁₀x + 4 oe (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Hence or otherwise express y in the form px^q
parts.final_form: equation y = 10000x^(−2/3) (not just p and q)
parts.ms: M1 one correct log law; dM1 full undo of logs to y = x^a × 10^b; A1 y = 10 000x^(−2/3). Partly correct answer with no working: SC 100 (MS pp.8–9)

parts.ask: f(x) = (2x + 5)²/(x − 3), x ≠ 3: find f′(x) as P(x)/Q(x) with fully factorised quadratics
parts.ms: M1 quotient (or product) rule form; A1 correct unsimplified; M1 take out the factor (2x + 5) (or expand and factorise the numerator); A1 (2x + 5)(2x − 17)/(x − 3)² (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Hence find the range of values of x for which f(x) is increasing
parts.ms: M1 both critical values from the numerator (or one correct end); A1 x < −2.5, x > 8.5; final answer marked, not isw (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: g(x) = x√(sin 4x), 0 ≤ x < π/4, maximum at M: show x_M satisfies tan 4x + kx = 0
parts.ms: M1 chain rule on (sin 4x)^(1/2); M1 product rule; A1 (sin 4x)^(1/2) + 2x(sin 4x)^(−1/2)cos 4x; M1 set = 0 and multiply by (sin 4x)^(1/2)/cos 4x; A1 cso tan 4x + 2x = 0. Alt: square first and differentiate implicitly (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Use t = tan x to show 12tan 2x + 5cot x sec²x = 0 can be written 5t⁴ − 24t² − 5 = 0
parts.final_form: given quartic, correct intermediate line, no notation errors
parts.ms: B1 one correct identity (tan 2x = 2t/(1 − t²), cot x = 1/t, sec²x = 1 + t²); M1 all three used to an equation in t; A1 correct intermediate equation; A1* given answer with "= 0", no notation slips such as tan x² for tan²x (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Hence solve for 0 ≤ x < 360°, showing each stage, to 1 d.p.
parts.ms: M1 solve the quadratic in t² ((5t² + 1)(t² − 5) = 0); dM1 tan x = ±√5 then x (tan x = 5 is M0); A1 two of 66°, 114°, 246°, 294°; A1 all four to 1 d.p., no extras (MS p.12)

parts.ask: f(x) = 2|2x − 5| + 3, x ≥ 0 (Figure 2): state the coordinates of the vertex P
parts.ms: B1 one coordinate; B1 (2.5, 3); reversed (3, 2.5) SC 10 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Solve f(x) = 3x − 2
parts.ms: M1 one correct modulus-free equation (signs correct); A1 5 or 15/7; dM1 both; A1 both, no extras. Squaring alt: 7x² − 50x + 75 = 0 (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: f(x) = kx + 2 has exactly two roots: find the range of values of k
parts.ms: M1 line through (0, 2) and P(2.5, 3), or k < 4 (gradient of the right arm); A1 critical value 2/5; A1 2/5 < k < 4 (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: y = 2cos 3x − 3x + 4, x > 0 (radians), crosses the x-axis at x = α: show α lies between 0.8 and 0.9
parts.final_form: two values, sign change, continuity, conclusion
parts.ms: M1 y at 0.8 and 0.9, one correct to 1 s.f. (0.13, −0.51); A1 both, "change of sign, continuous" and conclusion (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Using x_{n+1} = (1/3)arccos(1.5xₙ − 2) with x₁ = 0.8, find x₂ to 4 d.p.
parts.ms: M1 substitute 0.8; A1 awrt 0.8327 (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Find x₅ to 4 d.p.
Q and R are the two smallest-x local minima, at x = β and x = λ: find their exact values using calculus
parts.ms: M1 dy/dx = A sin 3x + B; A1 −6sin 3x − 3; dM1 dy/dx = 0, sin 3x = −1/2, arcsin then ÷3; A1 one of 7π/18, 19π/18; ddM1 third positive solution for λ; A1 β = 7π/18 and λ = 19π/18, correctly labelled (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Find by algebraic integration the exact value of ∫ from 3 to 42 of 2/(3x − 1) dx, in simplest form
parts.ms: M1 k ln(3x − 1); A1 (2/3)ln(3x − 1); dM1 both limits and one log law; A1 (2/3)ln(25/4) or equivalent (e.g. (4/3)ln(5/2)) (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: h(x) = (2x³ − 7x² + 8x + 1)/(x − 1)², x > 1, = Ax + B + C/(x − 1)²: find ∫h(x) dx
parts.ms: B1 one of A = 2, B = −3, C = 4; M1 full method for A, B, C (division or identity); A1 2x − 3 + 4/(x − 1)²; M1 ∫P/(x − 1)² → Q/(x − 1); A1ft (1/2)Ax² + Bx − C/(x − 1); A1 x² − 3x − 4/(x − 1) (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: f(θ) = 5cos θ − 4sin θ: express as R cos(θ + α), R > 0, 0 < α < π/2; exact R, α in radians to 3 d.p.
parts.ms: B1 R = √41 (decimals not accepted for this mark); M1 tan α = ±4/5 or ±5/4; A1 awrt 0.675 (degrees A0) (MS p.19)

parts.ask: y = cos θ is mapped to y = f(θ) by a stretch then a translation: describe the stretch fully
parts.final_form: stretch parallel to the y-axis, scale factor √41
parts.ms: B1ft stretch in the y direction by √41 (size and direction needed; "translated by √41" is B0) (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: Describe the translation fully
parts.final_form: translation by 0.675 in the negative x direction
parts.ms: B1ft translate left by 0.675 (vector (−0.675, 0)); "left by −0.675" or no direction is B0; both correct but unlabelled SC B1 B0 (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: g(θ) = 90/(4 + (f(θ))²): find the range of g
parts.ms: M1 one end by a correct method (90/4 or 90/(4 + 41)); A1 2 ≤ g ≤ 22.5 (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ms: M1 cross-multiply and collect x terms; A1 (4x − 3)/(x − 5) oe; B1 domain x > 5 (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Find a and b to 3 significant figures
parts.ms: B1 a = 10^3.08 = awrt 1200; M1 log₁₀b = their gradient; A1 b = awrt 1.43. (a) and (b) marked together (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: When t = T there are 500 000 subscribers: find T according to the model
parts.final_form: value awrt 17 (not left as a log)
parts.ms: M1 solve 1200 × 1.43ᵀ = 500 000 or log₁₀500 000 = 3.08 + 0.154T; A1 awrt 17, only if (a) or (b) correct (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: f(x) = |kx − 9| − 2, k > 0 (Figure 2): find the y coordinate of A (y-intercept)
parts.ms: B1 7 ((0, 7) condoned, not (7, 0)) (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of k, the x coordinate of the minimum point B
Find, in terms of k, the values of x satisfying |kx − 9| − 2 < 0
parts.ms: M1 both critical values from kx − 9 = ±2 (or −2 < kx − 9 < 2, or squaring); A1 7/k and 11/k; A1 7/k < x < 11/k as one statement ("or", or two separate inequalities not joined, not accepted) (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: The line y = 3 − 2x meets y = f(x) at two distinct points: find the range of possible values of k

parts.ask: All stages shown: f(x) = 5(x² − 2)(4x + 9)^(1/2), x ≥ −9/4; show f′(x) = k(5x² + 9x − 2)/(4x + 9)^(1/2), integer k
parts.ms: M1 product rule A(5x² − 10)(4x + 9)^(−1/2) ± Bx(4x + 9)^(1/2); A1 correct unsimplified; dM1 single fraction, expand numerator to a 3TQ (not straight to the given quadratic); A1 10(5x² + 9x − 2)/(4x + 9)^(1/2), no errors (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: Hence find the values of x for which f′(x) = 0
parts.ms: B1 x = −2, 1/5 (withheld if one is rejected) (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: C has a local maximum at P: find the exact coordinates of P
parts.ms: M1 substitute the smaller root into f; A1 (−2, 10) only. (b) and (c) marked together (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: g(x) = 2f(x) + 4, −9/4 ≤ x ≤ 0: find the range of g
parts.ms: B1 f(0) = −30; M1 2 × 10 + 4 as upper or 2 × (−30) + 4 as lower bound (not 2f(1/5) + 4); A1 −56 ≤ g(x) ≤ 24 (−56 ≤ f ≤ 24 or "or" forms not accepted) (MS pp.17–19)

parts.ask: All stages shown: show 2sin θ(3cot²2θ − 7) = 13sec θ can be written 3cosec²2θ − 13cosec 2θ − 10 = 0
parts.final_form: given quadratic in cosec 2θ, no errors or notation slips
parts.ms: M1 divide by 2sin θ and use sec θ = 1/cos θ, or replace cot²2θ by cosec²2θ − 1; dM1 both; ddM1 sin 2θ = 2sin θ cos θ and collect to a 3TQ in cosec 2θ; A1* no errors, sin θ cos θ or sin 2θ seen; poor notation (cosec²2θ written wrongly, missing 2 in 2θ) loses A1 (MS pp.20–21)

parts.ask: Hence solve for 0 < θ < π/2, answers to 3 s.f.
parts.final_form: two solutions in radians to 3 s.f. (0.101, 1.47)
parts.ms: M1 solve the quadratic, reciprocal of a root; A1 sin 2θ = 1/5; dM1 arcsin then divide by 2; A1 awrt 0.101, 1.47, no others in range; intermediate working required (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: Sprinter: v = 12 − e^(t − 10) − 12e^(−0.75t), t ≥ 0: using calculus, find the maximum velocity
parts.final_form: max velocity awrt 11.9 m s⁻¹ (t = (10 + ln 9)/1.75 ≈ 6.97); calculus must be seen
parts.ms: M1 dv/dt = −e^(t − 10) + 9e^(−0.75t) = 0; A1 9 = e^(1.75t − 10) oe; M1 solve with correct logs for t; A1 awrt 6.97; A1 awrt 11.9. No calculus: 0 marks (MS pp.22–23)

parts.final_form: given equation T = …, no bracket errors
parts.ms: M1 integrate to 12t ± Ae^(t − 10) ± Be^(−0.75t); A1 12t − e^(t − 10) + 16e^(−0.75t); M1 limits T and 0, = 100, make 12T the subject; A1* given result (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: Using the iteration with T₁ = 10, find T₂ to 4 decimal places
parts.ms: M1 substitute 10; A1 awrt 9.7493 (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: Find, to 4 d.p., the time taken to run the race according to the model
parts.final_form: 4 d.p.: 9.7293 s (by iteration, not direct calculator solving)
parts.ms: A1 9.7293 (needs the method mark). SC over-rounding to 9.749 and 9.729: M1A0A1 (MS p.23)

parts.ask: All stages shown: y = (1 + 2cos x)/(1 + sin x), −π/2 < x < 3π/2, minimum at M: show the x coordinate of M satisfies 2sin x + cos x = −2
parts.ms: M1 quotient (or product) rule form; A1 correct derivative; dM1 numerator = 0, expand, use sin²x + cos²x = 1 to an equation with no squared terms; A1* 2sin x + cos x = −2. Using only vu′ − uv′ numerator throughout: max M1A0dM1A0 (MS pp.24–25)

parts.ask: Hence find, to 3 s.f., the x coordinate of M
parts.final_form: single value awrt 3.79 (radians); answer only scores 0
parts.ms: R-method: M1 R = √5; M1 α = arctan(1/2) or arctan 2; A1 √5 sin(x + 0.464) = −2 or √5 cos(x − 1.107) = −2; dM1 solve for x; A1 awrt 3.79 only. Squaring, tan or t-substitution routes marked equivalently (MS pp.24–27)

parts.ask: All stages shown, no calculator-only solutions: f(x) = (2x³ − 4x − 15)/(x² + 3x + 4); show f(x) ≡ Ax + B + C(2x + 3)/(x² + 3x + 4) with integers A, B, C
parts.ms: M1 long division or multiply through and compare coefficients (A = 2 implies); A1 A = 2; A1 B = −6 or C = 3; A1 both (MS p.7)
parts.er: Long division most common and most successful; quotient 2x alone earned 2 of 4; comparing coefficients less successful through algebra errors; some left Q1 blank (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Hence find the integral of f(x) from 3 to 5, in the form p + ln q with integers p, q
parts.ms: M1 integrate their (a): xⁿ → xⁿ⁺¹ and (2x + 3)/(x² + 3x + 4) → k ln(x² + 3x + 4); A1ft x² − 6x + 3ln(x² + 3x + 4); dM1 apply limits and subtract; M1 combine logs to one term; A1 cao 4 + ln 8. Letters A, B, C left in: max M1A1ft dM0 M1 A0 (MS p.7)
parts.er: Some missed the f′(x)/f(x) form so had no log term; wrong k (often 1/3); about half of those reaching 4 + 3ln 2 lost the last mark by not writing 3ln 2 as ln 8 (form required) (ER p.3)

parts.ask: f(x) = 5 − 4/(3x + 2), x ≥ 0: find the range of f
parts.final_form: inequality with correct strict/non-strict ends (3 ≤ f(x) < 5)
parts.ms: M1 one correct end (f(x) < 5 or f(x) ≥ 3); A1 3 ≤ f(x) < 5 (y allowed; x only in formal set notation) (MS p.8)
parts.er: Only a minority found both ends: most substituted x = 0 for one end, few sketched; inequality signs often wrong (ER pp.3–4)

parts.ask: Find f⁻¹(x)
parts.ms: M1 make x (or swapped y) the subject, correct order of operations; A1 f⁻¹(x) = (1/3)(4/(5 − x) − 2) oe, e.g. (2x − 6)/(15 − 3x) (MS p.8)
parts.er: Routine for most; common slip not multiplying every term by (3x + 2); a few confused f⁻¹ with f′ (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Write down the domain of f⁻¹
parts.final_form: domain in x (= range of f)
parts.ms: B1ft 3 ≤ x < 5 following (a); not 3 ≤ f⁻¹(x) < 5 or in y (MS p.8)
parts.er: Many re-derived a domain from scratch as if the domain were all reals instead of using the range of f (ER p.4)

parts.ask: g(x) = |4sin(x/3 + π/6)|, x ∈ ℝ: find fg(−π)
parts.ms: M1 evaluate g(−π) = |4sin(−π/6)| = 2 and substitute into f; A1 9/2 (decimal accepted; changing to degrees not isw) (MS p.8)
parts.er: Mostly correct; errors: using π for −π, ignoring the modulus (giving 6), calculator in degrees — "the use of π is always an indicator that radians are in use" (ER p.4)

parts.ask: All stages shown: f(x) = (x − 2)²e³ˣ has a maximum at A and a minimum at (2, 0); use calculus to find the exact coordinates of A
parts.ms: M1 product rule to α(x − 2)e³ˣ + β(x − 2)²e³ˣ; A1 correct derivative; M1 set = 0, remove e³ˣ (and x − 2, or solve 3x² − 10x + 8 = 0) and solve; A1 x = 4/3; A1 y = (4/9)e⁴ (MS p.9)
parts.er: Well answered; some multiplied the two derivatives; some did not find y; more lost the last A1 by giving a rounded decimal instead of the exact value (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Given f(x) = k has at least two distinct roots, state the range of possible values of k
parts.ms: M1 one correct boundary (k > 0 or k ≤ their y_A); A1ft 0 < k ≤ (4/9)e⁴ (awrt 24.3 accepted) (MS p.9)
parts.er: Many had one end right but lost the A mark for a wrong strict/non-strict sign or direction (ER p.4)

parts.ask: y = log₁₀(2x + 1): express x in terms of y
parts.ms: M1 undo the log (10ʸ = 2x + 1) and rearrange; A1 x = (10ʸ − 1)/2, isw (MS p.10)
parts.er: Mostly correct; errors log y = 2x + 1, or "simplifying" (10ʸ − 1)/2 wrongly, or working with eʸ (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Hence find dy/dx, giving the answer in terms of x
parts.ms: M1 dx/dy = (1/2)10ʸ ln 10; M1 dy/dx = 1/(dx/dy), variables consistent; A1 2/((2x + 1)ln 10). Alts: change of base y = ln(2x + 1)/ln 10 then chain rule; implicit differentiation. No ln 10 term: M0M1A0 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Reciprocal step the safest mark; differentiation of 10ʸ the main problem (10ʸ⁻¹, or a factor ln y); some left the answer in y — check the rubric; implicit differentiation common and usually successful (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Profit model P = (4t − 1)/10 + (3/4)ln[(t + 1)/(2t + 1)²] (£ million, t years): show that after exactly one year there was a loss of about £830 000
parts.final_form: value of P(1) then conclusion stating a loss in £
parts.ms: M1 substitute t = 1; A1* P(1) = −0.828… so a loss of about £830 000; must say "loss" and give units; a negative value given as the answer is A0 (MS pp.11–12)
parts.er: Most accessed mark on the paper; accuracy often lost by omitting £ or not saying "loss", or by never evaluating P (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Show that the value of t for which P = 0 lies in [6, 7]
parts.final_form: two values, sign change, continuity, conclusion
parts.ms: M1 P(6) and P(7), at least one correct to 1 s.f. (−0.0880, 0.198); A1 both correct, sign change, continuity and conclusion (MS pp.11–12)
parts.er: Accuracy mostly lost for no reference to continuity — "the case for the past few series"; teach continuity as a vital part (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Show that P = 0 can be written t = 1/4 + (15/8)ln[(2t + 1)/(t + 1)]
parts.final_form: given equation, with an intermediate step
parts.ms: M1 isolate the t term from (4t − 1)/10 after setting P = 0; A1* given form with no errors and an intermediate step (power law on the log or t = … seen) (MS pp.11–12)
parts.er: Errors handling the sign change and power law on the log term; insufficient steps for a given answer (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Using the iteration with t₁ = 6, find t₂ and t₆ to 3 decimal places
parts.ms: M1 use the formula with t₁ = 6; A1 awrt 6.220 (6.22 accepted); A1 t₆ = 6.314 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Generally well answered; most common loss 6.13 for t₆ (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Hence find how many months it takes, from the start of trading, for the company to make a profit
parts.final_form: whole number of months in context (76)
parts.ms: M1 multiply their root by 12 (or fractional part × 12); A1 75 or awrt 76 months (MS pp.11–12)
parts.er: Many took t as months or did not multiply by 12, leaving 6.3 years or "7 months" (ER pp.5–6)

parts.ask: y = (2 + 3sin x)/(cos x + sin x): show dy/dx = (a tan x + b sec x + c)/(sec x + 2sin x) with integers a, b, c
parts.final_form: given form with integers (2tan x + 3sec x − 2)/(sec x + 2sin x)
parts.ms: B1 d/dx(cos x + sin x) = −sin x + cos x; M1 quotient (or product) rule; A1 correct derivative; M1 expand and use sin²x + cos²x = 1 (to 3 + 2sin x − 2cos x over 1 + 2sin x cos x); M1 multiply numerator and denominator by sec x; A1 a = 2, b = 3, c = −2 (MS p.13)
parts.er: Discriminating; quotient rule mostly right (some subtracted the wrong way round); expansion slips (losing the 3) blocked the identity; many stopped after the quotient rule; needed both the Pythagorean identity and multiplying by sec x (ER p.6)

parts.ask: C₁: y = 5 − |3x − 22| (Figure 3): write down the coordinates of the vertex
parts.ms: B1 (22/3, 5); (a) and (b) marked as a whole (MS pp.14–15)
parts.er: Mostly right; some gave only x = 22/3 or (22/3, 0) (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Write down the coordinates of the intersection of C₁ with the y-axis
parts.er: A number wrote −17 alone with no indication it was the y value and lost the mark (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the x coordinates of the intersections of C₁ with the x-axis
parts.er: Mostly correct (calculator allowed here); some solved only one case (ER p.6)

parts.ask: On Diagram 1 sketch C₂: y = (1/9)x² − 9, labelling intersections with the axes
parts.final_form: U-shape symmetric about y-axis through (±9, 0) and (0, −9), meeting C₁ at (9, 0)
parts.ms: B1 U shape symmetric about the y-axis, vertex on negative y-axis; B1 meets C₁ at (9, 0) with (−9, 0) also shown; B1 (0, −9) labelled (MS pp.14–15)
parts.er: Mostly correct; wrong shapes: straight line, V-shape, inverted parabola; a few drew the intersection at x = 17/3 (ER p.7)

parts.ask: No calculator-only solutions: find the coordinates of the points of intersection of C₁ and C₂
parts.final_form: exactly two points (9, 0) and (3, −8); larger root rejected
parts.ms: B1 (9, 0) deduced; M1 5 + (3x − 22) = (1/9)x² − 9; dM1 solve (x − 3)(x − 24) = 0; dM1 choose the smaller root x = 3 and find y; A1 (3, −8) only. Alt: square to a quartic. Calculator-only answers: max B1 (MS pp.14–15)
parts.er: Many solved the wrong branch (x = 9, −36) and gave (−36, y); others missed (9, 0); x = 24 not rejected; extra solutions cost the last two marks (ER p.7)

parts.ask: All stages shown: given cos 2θ − sin 3θ ≠ 0, prove cos²θ/(cos 2θ − sin 3θ) ≡ (1 + sin θ)/(1 − 2sin θ − 4sin²θ)
parts.final_form: proof reaching the given identity with no errors
parts.ms: M1 compound angle on sin 3θ = sin(2θ + θ) (or 3sin θ − 4sin³θ); M1 double angle formulae to single angles; M1 Pythagorean identity to expose the factor (1 − sin θ) in the numerator (cos²θ = (1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)); A1* cancel 1 − sin θ, no errors. Alts: work in reverse, or cross-multiply to a true statement with conclusion (MS pp.17–19)
parts.er: Hardest part of the paper; first two Ms accessible but few saw the Pythagorean identity and difference of two squares; typically 0–2 marks (ER p.8)

parts.ask: Hence solve cos²θ/(cos 2θ − sin 3θ) = 2cosec θ for 0 < θ ≤ 360°, to 1 d.p.
parts.final_form: all four solutions in degrees to 1 d.p.: 15.6°, 164.4°, 235.6°, 304.4°
parts.ms: M1 use (a) and cross-multiply to an equation in sin θ only; A1 9sin²θ + 5sin θ − 2 = 0; M1 solve and take arcsin of a root; A1 two of 15.6, 164.4, 235.6, 304.4; A1 all four, no others; radians A0 (MS p.17)
parts.er: Often skipped though routine; when tried mostly 4/5; last A1 lost for only two solutions or wrong rounding; misplacing the 2 gave the wrong quadratic (ER p.8)

parts.ms: M1 S = 10^(4.5 - 0.012); A1 awrt 30 800 km^2 (units needed).
parts.er: Units most often missing (ER p.6).

parts.ask: Complete equation S = pq^t with p and q to 3 s.f.

parts.er: q the most discriminating value; sign errors splitting the power; p and q given without the equation (ER p.6).

parts.ask: With reference to the model, interpret q.
parts.ms: B1 proportion of sea floor area covered by coral retained each year (falls by 1.4% per year); must mention area/sea floor, coral, per year, proportion. 'Rate of change' or 'gradient' not accepted.
parts.er: Least-scored mark of the paper: absolute change per year given, or p interpreted instead (ER p.6).

parts.er: Rarely reached without the correct form in (c); graphical-calculator answers not credited (ER pp.10-12).

parts.ms: B1 3x^2 + 7x - 20 = (3x - 5)(x + 4); M1 combine over a correct common denominator; A1* no errors.
parts.er: Usually well done; factor 2 lost when factorising 2x^2 - 32; calculator-style factors (x - 5/3) caused trouble (ER pp.5-6).

parts.ask: Using calculus, f is a decreasing function; reasoning must be clear.
parts.ms: M1 quotient/product rule; A1 correct derivative; A1cso* f'(x) = -10/(3x - 5)^2 < 0 because (3x - 5)^2 > 0, so decreasing.
parts.er: Final mark gained by a minority: no comment, or 'negative' without the squared denominator, or no conclusion; some ignored 'using calculus' and compared values (ER pp.5-6).

parts.ms: M1 rearrange to x = e^(...); A1 e^((x - 3)/2); B1 domain x >= 3.
parts.er: Errors: using 3 + ln x, wrong order, answer left in y or called f^-1; correct domain x >= 3 rarely seen (ER pp.5-6).

parts.ask: Exact a with gf(a) = 5.
parts.ms: B1 3 + 2 ln(2a/(3a - 5)) = 5; M1 ln(...) = 1 then 2a/(3a - 5) = e; dM1 make a the subject; A1 a = 5e/(3e - 2).
parts.er: Forming fg instead of gf; splitting the ln as a subtraction before exponentiating; decimals instead of e cost the last marks (ER pp.5-6).

parts.ask: Banner: show all stages of working; solutions relying entirely on calculator technology not acceptable. Room temperature T = 10 + Ae^(-Bt) deg C; 18 deg C at switch-off: A.
parts.er: Little difficulty (ER pp.6-7).

parts.ask: 16 deg C after 45 minutes: B.
parts.ms: M1 16 = 10 + 8e^(-45B) to e^(-45B) = ...; dM1 logs to B; A1 awrt 0.00639 (correct answer only scores 0).
parts.er: Some rounded to 0.006 (3 d.p., not 3 s.f.); 6.39 misread from standard form (ER pp.6-7).

parts.ask: Rate of change of temperature exactly 2 minutes after switch-off, deg C per minute.
parts.ms: M1 dT/dt = k e^(-Bt) at t = 2; A1 -0.0505 (or 0.0505 decreasing).
parts.er: Some substituted instead of differentiating (17.89) or used an average rate; lost minus sign in the index; s.f. errors (-0.050) (ER pp.6-7).

parts.ask: Why the temperature cannot fall to 5 deg C according to the model.
parts.ms: B1 lower limit/asymptote of 10 deg C, or e^(-Bt) = -5/8 has no solution (log of a negative number).
parts.er: Reasons split between the two routes; 'maximum temperature is 10' or 'logs cannot be negative' not accepted; minimum given as 8 or 18 (ER pp.6-7).

parts.ask: Banner: show all stages of working; solutions relying entirely on calculator technology not acceptable. y = 16/(9(3x - k)), x > k/3, k > 0, k != 3: dy/dx in simplest form in terms of k.
parts.ms: M1 A(3x - k)^-2; A1 -16/(3(3x - k)^2) (no common factor left).
parts.er: Chain rule on the unexpanded form was most successful; expanded denominators (9 x 3 = 18) and quotient/product rule attempts went wrong; some integrated (ER pp.7-9).

parts.ask: Gradient at P (x = 1) is -12: the two possible values of k.
parts.ms: M1 derivative = -12 rearranged to (3x - k)^2 = ...; dM1 x = 1 and solve (A < 0 needed); A1 k = 7/3, 11/3 (exact).
parts.er: Accessible; expanding the square was longer and error-prone (ER pp.7-9).

parts.ask: Given k < 3: normal at P as ax + by + c = 0, integers.
parts.ms: M1 y at P with their k (8/3); dM1 normal with gradient 1/12; A1 12y - x - 31 = 0.
parts.er: x = 1 not used, k used as the gradient, gradient +/- 12 used for the normal; non-integer coefficients (ER pp.7-9).

parts.ask: Using algebraic integration, integral from 1 to 3 of 16/(9(3x - k)) dx = lambda ln 10.
parts.ms: M1 B ln(3x - k); A1ft (16/27) ln(3x - 7/3); dM1 limits 3 and 1; A1 (16/27) ln 10.
parts.er: Coefficient errors from integrating by inspection; unchanged limits with substitution; 'ln 10' claimed when it did not follow (ER pp.7-9).
